name: weekend-hike
description: Seven people, three candidate times. Shows the four cases a merge can get wrong: disagreement, half a commitment, three different kinds of not-reached, and one person the address book cannot call at all.
_numbers: Placeholders from the reserved +1 555 555 01xx range. The live path additionally refuses every number that appears in a bundled fixture.
_proof: This is the scenario behind 'ringedingeding proof'. Vera is scripted with a number here because a fixture describes CALLS; whether the address book knows her number is a project-layer fact. The core sample deliberately enters her WITHOUT one and adds it afterwards, which is how the catch-up is demonstrated.

poll.question: It is about the hike this weekend. Which of these times could you make?

nora.summary: Nora can make both Saturday windows, Sunday does not work.
nora.transcript:
[00:04] BOT: This is an automated call on behalf of the organizer.
[00:11] USER: Sure, go ahead.
[00:19] USER: Saturday is fine either way. Sunday I am away.

paul.summary: Paul can make Saturday morning and Sunday, not Saturday afternoon.
paul.transcript:
[00:05] BOT: This is an automated call on behalf of the organizer.
[00:16] USER: Saturday afternoon is out, I work. Morning yes, Sunday yes.

rike.summary: Rike named Saturday morning and said nothing about the other two.

structured_result.note: Has to check the rest with her partner.

rike.transcript:
[00:06] BOT: This is an automated call on behalf of the organizer.
[00:14] USER: Saturday morning works. The rest I have to check with my partner first.

sven.summary: Sven picked up and said he did not want to answer this on the phone.
sven.transcript:
[00:04] BOT: This is an automated call on behalf of the organizer.
[00:09] USER: I would rather not do this with a machine, sorry.
[00:12] BOT: Understood. Thank you, goodbye.

vera.transcript:
[00:05] BOT: This is an automated call on behalf of the organizer.
[00:15] USER: Saturday I am at a wedding, the whole day. Sunday morning would work.
